title: Do two triangular 2×2 matrices generate a free semigroup? Decide it
credit: Cassaigne–Harju–Karhumäki (1999) and Cassaigne–Nicolas (2012), Open Question 8 and the (λ,μ) reduction.
premise_risks: The claim that every two-generator upper-triangular rational instance reduces to the (λ,μ) family is from Cassaigne–Nicolas; the formalized statement does not depend on it.
Decidability of FREE(2) over 2×2 N-matrices (Open Question 8) is a slightly different instance class; a solution of one may not immediately settle the other.
plain: For rational numbers λ and μ consider the matrices D = [[λ,0],[0,1]] and T = [[μ,1],[0,1]], or equivalently the maps x -> λx and x -> μx + 1 of the line. They are called free if different finite words in D and T always multiply to different matrices. Is there an algorithm that, given λ and μ, decides whether D and T are free? Deciding freeness of any two upper-triangular 2×2 rational matrices reduces to this family, and freeness is already undecidable for 3×3 matrices of natural numbers.
math: For $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb Q$ let $D_\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $T_\mu=\begin{pmatrix}\mu&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, and let $\phi_{\lambda,\mu}:\{0,1\}^*\to M_2(\mathbb Q)$ be the monoid morphism with $0\mapsto D_\lambda$ and $1\mapsto T_\mu$. Let $\Phi=\{(\lambda,\mu)\in\mathbb Q^2:\phi_{\lambda,\mu}\text{ is injective}\}$. Determine whether $\Phi$ is a decidable (recursive) subset of $\mathbb Q^2$. A proof of either answer settles the problem.
